title: 2 Chronicles 23
paragraphs: ¹ In the seventh year, Jehoiada showed his resolve and made a covenant with the commanders of hundreds: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri. ² They traveled throughout Judah and gathered the Levites from all the towns of Judah and the heads of Israelite families. They came to Jerusalem, ³ and the whole assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of God. Jehoiada said to them, "The king's son shall reign, just as the LORD promised concerning David's descendants. ⁴ Here is what you must do: a third of you priests and Levites who come on duty on the Sabbath are to be gatekeepers, ⁵ a third shall be at the palace, and a third at the Foundation Gate — and all the people shall be in the courtyards of the house of the LORD."

⁶ "Let no one enter the house of the LORD except the priests and the Levites on duty; they may enter because they are holy. All the other people are to carry out the LORD's assignment. ⁷ The Levites are to station themselves around the king, each with his weapons in his hand. Anyone who tries to enter the house must be put to death. Stay close to the king wherever he goes." ⁸ The Levites and all the men of Judah did everything that Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each brought his men — those coming on duty on the Sabbath and those going off duty — for Jehoiada the priest had not dismissed the divisions. ⁹ Then Jehoiada the priest issued the spears and the large and small shields that had belonged to King David and were kept in the house of God. ¹⁰ He stationed all the people with their weapons in hand, from the south side of the house to the north side, surrounding the altar and the house, to guard the king on every side.

¹¹ Then they brought out the king's son and put the crown on him. They gave him the covenant and proclaimed him king. Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and shouted, "Long live the king!" ¹² When Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and cheering the king, she came to them in the house of the LORD. ¹³ She looked, and there was the king standing by his pillar at the entrance. The commanders and trumpeters were beside him, and all the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and the singers with their musical instruments were leading the praise. Then Athaliah tore her robes and cried out, "Treason! Treason!" ¹⁴ Jehoiada the priest said to the commanders who were in charge of the troops, "Bring her out to the outer precincts and put to the sword anyone who follows her" — for the priest had said, "Do not put her to death at the house of the LORD." ¹⁵ So they seized her, and when she reached the entrance of the Horse Gate on the palace grounds, they put her to death there.

¹⁶ Jehoiada then made a covenant between himself and the people and the king, that they would be the LORD's people. ¹⁷ All the people went to the temple of Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars. ¹⁸ Then Jehoiada placed the oversight of the house of the LORD in the hands of the Levitical priests, whom David had assigned to the LORD's house, to present burnt offerings to the LORD as written in the Law of Moses, with rejoicing and singing, as David had prescribed. ¹⁹ He also stationed gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the LORD so that no one who was in any way unclean might enter. ²⁰ He took with him the commanders of hundreds, the nobles, the rulers of the people, and all the people of the land, and together they brought the king down from the house of the LORD. They came through the Upper Gate into the palace and seated the king on the royal throne.
²¹ All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet, now that Athaliah had been put to the sword.
